messages.author: b0d73bbd2c387b6c
messages.subject: Estimation Scores: Numerical vs. Analytical
parts:
Dear Yves,
 
I currently use the lavaan function for structural equational modeling and apply afterwards predict to get the scores.
 
Recently I read Joereskorg's paper on "Latent Variable Scores and Their Uses" which derives an analytical
representation of the scores (based on some matrix algebra, svd etc.).
I now also calculated the scores using Joereskorg's representation but did not get the same result than the predict function.
 
I realized that this might be due to the fact that lavaan uses the built-in optimizer nlminb, and I was wondering why
an optimizer is used in the algorithm and not the explicit representation of the scores?
 
Thanks for your help and regards,
Sonja

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Estimation Scores: Numerical vs. Analytical
parts:
On 11/04/2013 12:46 PM, Sonja wrote:
> Dear Yves,
> I currently use the lavaan function for structural equational
> modeling and apply afterwards predict to get the scores.
> Recently I read Joereskorg's paper on "Latent Variable Scores and Their
> Uses" which derives an analytical
> representation of the scores (based on some matrix algebra, svd etc.).
> I now also calculated the scores using Joereskorg's representation but
> did not get the same result than the predict function.
> I realized that this might be due to the fact that lavaan uses the
> built-in optimizer nlminb, and I was wondering why
> an optimizer is used in the algorithm and not the explicit
> representation of the scores?

The paper only discusses factor scores for the continuous case. The
difference between lavaan and LISREL is that LISREL transforms the
factor scores in such a way that their mean vector and covariance matrix
coincides with the model-implied mean and covariances of the latent
variables. In lavaan, we use the more traditional formulas as described
in Lawley & Maxwell (1971). See also Appendix 11 of the Mplus technical
appendices:

http://www.statmodel.com/download/techappen.pdf

For continuous data, nlminb() is not used. We only need to 'optimize' in
the categorical case (again, see Appendix 11 of the Mplus technical
appendices, eq 231: we need to 'minimize' this one).

Hope this helps,

Yves.
